extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent prosecutors, and patent practitioners advising on reexamination
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluative standards for handling citation of prior art and the scope, examination, and procedural requirements of ex parte reexamination (including reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304 and 257).

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing of cited prior art on PTO forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must list on form PTO-892 (or, if already listed, on PTO/SB/08 or PTO/SB/42 or equivalent) all prior art patents or printed publications cited in the decision on the request, applied in making rejections, or cited as pertinent during reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited prior art may have come from (A) prior art submissions under 37 CFR 1.501 received before the order, (B) earlier examination proceedings, or (C) examiner-discovered prior art. All citations listed on PTO-892 and all citations not lined-through on PTO/SB/08 or PTO/SB/42 will be the list of prior art documents considered in the reexamination proceeding; a notice will be printed on the reexamination certificate that the list is available via the USPTO electronic filing system by reexamination control number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for entry and citation of submitted patents/publications
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission of patents and/or publications is entitled to entry and citation in the reexamination certificate only when it complies with 37 CFR 1.98 and is submitted via certain specified routes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible submissions include: (A) by the patent owner in the statement under 37 CFR 1.530; (B) by the reexamination requester in the reply under 37 CFR 1.535; (C) prior to the order of reexamination under 37 CFR 1.501 by any party; and/or (D) by the patent owner under duty of disclosure requirements of 37 CFR 1.555.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of examination in ex parte reexamination (37 CFR 1.552(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in an ex parte reexamination proceeding will be examined on the basis of patents or printed publications and, with respect to subject matter added or deleted in the reexamination proceeding, on the basis of the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When new or amended subject matter is presented, enablement and written description under 35 U.S.C. 112 are applied to that amendatory matter; original claim matter is generally not reexamined under 112 except as specified elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: No enlargement of claim scope permitted (37 CFR 1.552(b) / 35 U.S.C. 305)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in ex parte reexamination will not be permitted to enlarge the scope of the claims of the patent; proposed amended or new claims enlarging scope are not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 305 states no proposed amended or new claim enlarging scope will be permitted. Examiner must reject any claim that enlarges scope under 35 U.S.C. 305 (use form paragraph 22.11). A claim 'enlarges the scope' if it is broader than each and every claim of the patent (see MPEP §1412.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on issues resolvable in reexamination (37 CFR 1.552(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues other than those indicated in 1.552(a) and (b) (patents/printed publications and enlargement) will not be resolved in a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such other issues are raised by the patent owner or third party during reexamination, the examiner should note their existence in the next Office action, and the patent owner may consider filing a reissue application to have those issues resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of patent owner statements to construe claims (37 CFR 1.552(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any statement of the patent owner and accompanying information submitted pursuant to 37 CFR 1.501(a)(2) that is of record may be used after reexamination has been ordered to determine the proper meaning of a patent claim when applying patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such statements are considered at the examination stage (after order) for claim interpretation in connection with prior art applied to the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental examination/reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 257: broader scope
rubrics_metrics.description: An ex parte reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257 is conducted under §§1.530–1.570 except that the owner has no right to file a §1.530 statement and reexamination may be conducted on the basis of any item of information under §1.605, not limited to patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination under 257 may consider issues beyond those in 1.552(a)/(c), may involve any ground of patentability (e.g., 101, anticipation, public use/sale, obviousness, written description, enablement, indefiniteness, double-patenting), and defines information material to patentability per §1.56(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 304: basis and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304 provides a reexamination of patent claims on the basis of prior art patents and printed publications; 35 U.S.C. 112 is addressed only with respect to new claims or amendatory subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any new or amended claims are examined to ensure they do not enlarge the scope of the original patent claims (see 35 U.S.C. 305). Double patenting issues may also be considered during such reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable prior art regime and effective filing dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The prior art regime under which the application for the patent was examined (first-inventor-to-file or first-to-invent) generally governs reexamination; exceptions arise when amended/new claims have effective filing dates on/after March 16, 2013 or when benefit claims to earlier applications are involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a new/amended claim has an effective filing date on/after March 16, 2013, reexamination is conducted under first-inventor-to-file rules. If a benefit claim to an earlier application with filing date before March 16, 2013 is made, reexamination may be under first-to-invent rules only if the prior application's written description provides adequate 35 U.S.C. 112 support for all relevant claims and claim presentations. See MPEP Chapter 700 for details and statutory text (35 U.S.C. 102) as applied to each regime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously considered prior art — use in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: After reexamination is ordered on a proper substantial new question (SNQ), the propriety of making a ground of rejection based on prior art previously considered by the Office is governed by MPEP §2258.01; combinations of previously considered art and newly cited art can support an SNQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law (e.g., In re Hiniker) supports that combinations including art before the original examiner and newly cited art can justify ordering reexamination if they raise an SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on matters other than patents/printed publications in 35 U.S.C. 304
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections in reexaminations ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304 will not be based on matters other than patents or printed publications (e.g., public use/sale, inventorship, 35 U.S.C. 101, conduct issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rejection relying on prior public use or sale or insufficiency of disclosure (as to original subject matter) cannot be made even if it references a prior art patent or printed publication; prior art patents/printed publications must be applied under the appropriate parts of 35 U.S.C. 102 and/or 103.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening patents/printed publications as prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections may be based on intervening patents or printed publications where the patent claims under reexamination are entitled only to the filing date of the patent and are not supported by an earlier foreign or U.S. application whose filing date is claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intervening patents/prints are prior art under cases like In re Ruscetta and In re van Langenhoven; the Office may perform 35 U.S.C. 112 written description priority analysis during reexamination (In re NTP). See MPEP §211.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting is cognizable in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Double patenting (over prior art patents or non-prior art patents) is appropriate for consideration in reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 302, and may form a basis for ordering reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 304 and for rejections during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should determine whether double patenting raises an SNQ when deciding on a request and should determine during examination whether a rejection based on double patenting is appropriate. Reexamination cannot be used to retroactively recover 35 U.S.C. 121 safe harbor by deleting subject matter not present in parent application (see In re Janssen).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of affidavits, declarations, and other written evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits/declarations or other written evidence that explain contents or pertinent dates of prior art may be considered in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In reexaminations ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304, any rejection must be based upon the prior art patents or printed publications as explained by such affidavits or declarations; the rejection cannot be based on the affidavits/declarations themselves as the substantive ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions by patent owner and their use
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissions by the patent owner of record or in a court record may be utilized in combination with a patent or printed publication in reexamination, but an admission alone may not establish an initial SNQ under 35 U.S.C. 303.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A submission under 35 U.S.C. 301 may include patent owner statements from court or Office proceedings; if relied upon in the request, the requester must explain how the statement is used to determine claim meaning per 37 CFR 1.510(b)(2). Admissions in the record are part of the scope/content of the prior art (Graham) and require no independent proof; third parties cannot submit admissions made outside the record or court. Under 35 U.S.C. 257, admissions need not be combined with patents or printed publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim interpretation standards in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Original patent claims in reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304 are examined only on the basis of prior art patents/printed publications applied under 35 U.S.C. 102/103; claim terms should be construed consistently with judicial interpretations and the broadest reasonable interpretation standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If related litigation has a judicial claim construction, examiner should acknowledge and assess consistency with the broadest reasonable construction and provide reasoning when adopting a different construction. During reexamination (including 257), claims are given the broadest reasonable interpretation consistent with the specification; limitations in the specification are not to be read into claims. For expired patents, Phillips standard (ordinary and customary meaning) applies. The statutory presumption of validity (35 U.S.C. 282) does not apply in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited scope for 35 U.S.C. 112 compliance in 304
rubrics_metrics.description: In reexaminations ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304, 35 U.S.C. 112 compliance (enablement and written description) should be considered only as to amendatory and new text presented in the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A term in an original patent claim cannot be examined as too broad under 112 unless the amendatory matter creates the issue. Rewriting a dependent claim as independent cannot be examined under 112 unless the rewriting raises a new question (e.g., lack of antecedent). The Office may determine entitlement to a priority/benefit date and perform a 112 written description priority analysis (see In re NTP).

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. 112 issues in reexamination ordered under 257
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexaminations ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257 may involve any issues under 35 U.S.C. 112, not limited to matter added or deleted during reexamination, and may include original subject matter in the specification, claims, and drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should consider enablement, written description, and other 112 grounds across original and amended materials as necessary in 257 proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: New matter prohibition and written-description rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 305 provides for examination under 35 U.S.C. 132, which prohibits introduction of new matter into the disclosure; new matter added to claims should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, for failing written-description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should consider relationship between written description and new matter prohibition (see MPEP §2163.06); when new matter affects claim limitations, apply 112 rejection accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of the specification must meet 35 U.S.C. 112
rubrics_metrics.description: When the specification is amended in a reexamination proceeding, the examiner must ensure the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112 are met since amendments can redefine claim term scope and cause claims to be unclear or unsupported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to the specification can cause failure of claims to comply with 112 even where claim language is unchanged; examiner should assess and, if appropriate, reject claims under relevant 112 grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for determining claim enlargement (35 U.S.C. 305 / MPEP §1412.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim presented in reexamination 'enlarges the scope' of the patent where it is broader than each and every claim of the patent; a claim is broadened if it contains any conceivable product/process that would not have infringed the original patent, even if narrower in other respects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MPEP §1412.03 guidance to determine broadening; employ form paragraph 22.11 for rejections under 35 U.S.C. 305. Examiner should identify and explain the claim limitations that broaden the scope (see bracket 2 in form paragraph).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of patents under reexamination subject to prior Office or court decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where some patent claims have been the subject of a prior Office or court decision, the examiner should follow MPEP §2242; claims held invalid by a court should be identified as not subject to reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When grounds in a prior Office or federal court decision are not based on patents or printed publications and raise validity questions, the Office action should state that the claims have not been examined as to those non-patent/publication grounds (see 37 CFR 1.552(c) and cases like In re Knight). For handling dependent claims relying on claims not subject to reexamination, see MPEP §2260.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limited to 'live' claims and requester requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office's determination in both the order for reexamination and the examination stage will generally be limited to review of the 'live' claims for which reexamination has been requested; the requester must set forth pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requester fails to apply the art to certain claims per 37 CFR 1.510(b), those claims generally will not be reexamined. The Office has discretion to reexamine claims not requested on individual facts and may add claims during examination if intervening prior art raises an SNQ as to those claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction requirements not proper in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction requirements (i.e., requiring restriction to one invention) cannot be made in a reexamination proceeding since no statutory basis exists for restriction in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding claims to a 'separate and distinct' invention would be considered enlargement of the patent claims and is impermissible (see Ex parte Wikdahl and MPEP §1412.03).
